summary:
Your 4-week volume has essentially flatlined — 127 km versus 125 km the prior block, 9 runs each — which at face value looks like consolidation, but the composition tells a more useful story. The 44 km effort on June 8th anchors that period, and the current block has been built around shorter, more frequent outputs with the standout being last Saturday's 15.73 km at 4:49/km average, your sharpest sustained pace in recent weeks and a clear marker that aerobic speed is in good shape.

Today's 13.77 km at 5:48/km with HR 137 is a clean aerobic recovery or base-building effort — low drift relative to the effort, and it pairs well with Monday's 11.73 km at a similarly easy intensity. That's two consecutive days of moderate volume at controlled heart rate, which is exactly the kind of back-to-back durability work that compounds quietly over time.

Your lactate threshold is now logged at 4:24/km at 178 bpm as of today — no 30-day baseline yet to compare against, but that figure sits meaningfully faster than your half marathon PB pace of 4:18/km, which is consistent with the fitness suggested by the 4:49/km average last Saturday. Worth watching as that baseline builds.
